description.narrative: In Sierra Leone, agriculture is predominantly based on the Slash-and-burn principle, which leads to a loss of (forest) vegetation and soil fertility. It also contributes significantly to greenhouse gas emissions (GHG) and regional climate change. The project promoted regenerative and climate neutral agriculture through the establishment of four permaculture projects and four vegetable gardens in four pilot communities in the Koinadugu District in Sierra Leone. A total of two hundred farmers (two thirds being women) learned about climate-friendly farming methods through capacity training programmes. Alongside, 1.200 community members benefit from awareness raising campaigns on the impacts of climate change and possible adaptation solutions. In addition to reducing GHG emissions, the project contributed to increasing income and food security as well as counteracting environmental degradation in the agricultural sector.
